newsitem.title: USA: PECO sees Pa. substation back early 1997.
newsitem.headline: PECO sees Pa. substation back early 1997.

text.p: PECO Energy Co said Monday it expected a key power substation in a northern suburb of Philadelphia to resume full operation by early next year after a fire destroyed one of its transformers earlier this month.
"That transformer will be replaced some time after January 1," a company spokesman said, adding the fire was ignited by an equipment problem inside the Whitpain substation.
As the substation continues to operate at reduced capacity, constraints have been imposed to avoid overloading transmission lines running north and eastern of the Whitpain substation, he said.
"This morning's problem was getting limited flow by three 500 kilovott (KV) lines into 230 KV circuits going out on the other side," he said.

If demand in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool rises above a certain level, utilities are resorting to turning on their fuel oil and/or natural gas stations in southern PJM to stablize the grid and to compensate for the reduced supply from the Whitpain substation, industry sources said.

The transmission curb has at times split the PJM grid into two systems, pushing up daily PJM power prices since the movement of cheaper nuclear and coal-generated power eastward was restricted, they said.
The Whitpain substation transmits some of the output from the nearby 2,110 megawatt (MW) Limerick nuclear generating complex.
